editorial: If you have ever felt completely numb after a big loss, this movie will hit close to home. Jake Gyllenhaal plays an investment banker whose wife dies in a car crash, and instead of crying, he starts taking apart his fridge, his office, and eventually his whole life. He meets a customer service rep played by Naomi Watts, and their strange connection gives him a reason to feel again. The tone is darkly funny but also deeply sad, so do not expect a light comedy. The pacing is steady and character-driven, with lots of quiet moments that let you sit with his grief. The acting is excellent, especially Gyllenhaal, who makes you care about a guy who seems cold at first. The downside is that some scenes feel a bit slow, and the humor might not land for everyone. If you enjoy emotional dramas with a quirky edge, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Davis finally lets his grief out by demolishing his own house with a bulldozer, which he had been planning throughout the movie. This act of destruction becomes his way of breaking down the walls he built around his emotions. He also connects with Naomi Watts' character and her son, finding a new sense of family and hope. The movie ends with him moving forward, no longer numb, ready to rebuild his life from the rubble.
